result.cross_cluster_issues:
1) samus-bio, 'Samus: Samus Aran – raised by the Chozo on Zebes', last paragraph: 'When she returned years later as a bounty hunter, Mother Brain had turned against her makers, the Space Pirates held the planet...' This implies she first learned of the fall then. Per the manga, she came to Zebes with Kreatz and Mauk as a Federation Police officer during the Pirate takeover. There she confronted Mother Brain, was beaten by Ridley during a panic attack, saw Gray Voice die and escaped; only later did she leave the Federation and return as a bounty hunter. Suggested wording: 'She saw Zebes fall once already, as a Federation Police officer during the Pirate takeover (per the manga); when she returned years later as a bounty hunter, ...'. Sources: https://www.metroidwiki.org/wiki/Pyonchi ('Samus returned to Zebes with them [Kreatz and Mauk] ... the two escape Zebes'; Pyonchi went to Keaton only 'after Samus left the Federation'), plus the manga domain entries 'Mother Brain's betrayal of Zebes' and 'Samus's confrontation with Ridley and her trauma'.
2) dark-samus, 'Dark Samus: The return – Colossus, Phaaze and the Norion attack': 'raiders extracted Aurora Unit 313 and jettisoned the crew into space' is stated as fact. That is only the Pirates' own claim in the 'Taking Valhalla' log ('At the command of Dark Samus, we jettisoned the crew...'). Samus found many Marines' bodies aboard the wreck. It should be attributed to Pirate records, as prime3 'GFS Olympus and the Valhalla' already does. Sources: https://www.metroidwiki.org/wiki/G.F.S._Valhalla and https://www.metroidwiki.org/wiki/Space_Pirate_Data
3) timeline, 'Universe: Timeline of Samus's missions', Prime 4 line: 'flings Samus and Federation marines to Viewros ... the marines restrain him'. The five castaways included an engineer (Myles MacKenzie) and an android (VUE-995), so 'Federation personnel' or 'Federation companions' is more accurate (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metroid_Prime_4:_Beyond). Minor.
4) phazon, 'Phazon: Pirate Phazon operations and the Federation's PED program': says Pirate Metroid experiments 'yielded the Phazon-mutated Hunter and Fission strains'. The space-pirates fact-check found that Metroid Wiki credits neither strain to Pirate work, so the claim was removed there. Please verify, or hedge it.
5) Keys still on 3 entries, left as acceptable because each entry is about that subject: 'Federation Police' (federation Police entry, manga 'Samus's Federation Police years', samus-bio service entry) and 'Bermuda System' (federation-force Bermuda System entry, bestiary-prime 'Fauna of the Bermuda System', tech planets index). If a stricter cap is wanted, drop 'Federation Police' from samus-bio and 'Bermuda System' from the tech index.
6) Dating note for the timeline owner: official sources conflict on the year Sylux stole the Metroid. Nintendo's in-game Sylux logbook says Cosmic Year 20X5; Nintendo's 'The World' Databook prologue and the Nintendo Today text say 20X6. The timeline entry's 20X6 agrees with the databook and with Federation Force; no change needed there.
result.notes:
Contradiction calls:
- Sylux theft year: set to 20X6 in prime4 (3 entries) to match federation-force (Bermuda incident 20X6), the timeline entries, the Databook and Nintendo Today. The in-game logbook's 20X5 is also the year of the first Zebes mission, which comes before the whole Prime series. The conflict is recorded in each entry's notes.
- The egg-to-strain link is official (Databook prologue: Sylux took the hatchlings from eggs stored by the Federation, exploiting their imprinting, then cultured them into the host-controlling strain), so federation-force [5] now agrees with prime4 and metroids.
- Doomseye shield: no change. Wikipedia says the Force 'disables the Doomseye's force field' after defeating Samus, which fits the space-pirates wording.
- G.F.S. Aegis: real (Nintendo Life review); the Olympus is now dated as flagship 'during the Phazon crisis' instead of removing either ship.
- Prime 4 placement: both the Wikipedia/Nintendo position (between Other M and Fusion) and Retro's 'after Super Metroid' put Tanamaar after Ceres/Zebes. The space-pirates and federation lists were reordered on that basis.
- Checked and left alone: Ridley 'original life form of Zebes' (Metroid Wiki cites the Metroid manual p.39); Anthony freezing a Lava Golem (Metroid Wiki Anthony Higgs page); Delano 7 as a 'believed stolen Federation prototype' (Metroid Wiki Delano 7 page); Valhalla codes, then Leviathan battleship, then wormhole order (agrees with prime3).
- Prime 4 overlap among its own entries (Tanamaar attack, Chrono Tower ending) is spread out in 1–3 sentences per entry rather than whole paragraphs, so I did not trim it.

Style: no 'player', 'boss', 'level', 'cutscene', 'unlock' or 'upgrade' wording, no markdown emphasis and no bracketed citations remain in the editable files. 'Scan Visor logbook' is kept as in-universe equipment.

All five files reload with json.load. No titles changed, no entries deleted, all entries constant=false, key counts are 5–12. Other URLs used: https://www.metroidwiki.org/wiki/Sylux, https://www.metroidwiki.org/wiki/Delano_7, https://www.metroidwiki.org/wiki/Space_Pirate_Data, https://www.metroidwiki.org/wiki/Anthony_Higgs, https://www.metroidwiki.org/wiki/Gray_Voice, https://www.metroidwiki.org/wiki/Samus_Aran, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metroid_Prime:_Federation_Force, https://www.nintendo.co.jp/3ds/bcaj/index.html, https://omegametroid.com/metroid-prime-4-beyond-walkthrough/logbook-guide-biology/ (confirms the logbook's 20X5 wording).
